title: Chapter 144 — Delivery Damage to the Home
intro: Scratched hardwood floors, dinged door frames, cracked tiles. This is no longer about an appliance.

sections.title: Immediate Response
sections.content:
When the delivery crew damages the customer's home, the complaint is no longer about an appliance — it is about their house. Respond immediately.

Photos from all angles — taken before the crew leaves. Acknowledgment — do not argue fault on-site. 'I am documenting this right now and I will file the claim today.' Contact info for the customer to reach you directly — not a general line.

Do NOT say 'our insurance will handle it.' Say 'I am taking care of this personally.'

sections.title: The Repair Coordination
sections.content:
File the damage claim with your delivery company's insurance. Get a repair estimate from a qualified contractor. Keep the customer informed at every step.

Covering repair costs without argument is almost always cheaper than losing the customer, the review, and the referrals. A $300 floor repair versus a $30,000 lifetime customer — the math is not even close.

sections.title: Prevention
sections.content:
Floor runners and door protectors on every delivery. Crew training on navigating tight spaces. Pre-delivery path assessment for premium deliveries.

One incident per 100 deliveries is industry average. Reducing it to one per 200 through prevention saves thousands per year in claims and immeasurably more in customer trust.
